summary: **Bottom line (final validation, 21 Nov 2026):** every choice was made on 2006–2018 data and tested once on 2019–2026. The **price ranges are accurate** and are the page's main forecast. **Gold's direction could not be predicted** by any model, driver set or rule we tried, and the one 'profitable' pattern turned out to be a backtest artefact. Nothing on this page should be read as a promise of profit.

sections.title: 2. Direction models: tuned on 2006–2018, tested once on 2019–2026
sections.text: Candidates: logistic regression at 3 regularisation strengths and gradient boosting in 2 sizes, on the base (23) or expanded (40) driver set, at 4 horizons: 40 configurations. The configuration with the best probability score on 2006–2018 was frozen and then tested.

sections.title: 3. Range model upgrade tested
sections.text: A HAR volatility model built from intraday highs and lows plus GVZ, chosen on 2006–2018, changed the 2019–2026 interval score by only −0.2% to −4% (weekly and monthly) and +0.5–1% (daily). It also dropped monthly 90% accuracy from 86% to 84%. **Kept the simpler current model.** Measured accuracy of the live model: 80% range 78–80%, 90% range 86–89%.

sections.title: 5. Time-of-day and day-of-week signals (21 Nov 2026)
sections.text: Average return of gold futures by hour of day, measured on hourly bars from Jul 2024 to Sep 2025 and tested on Sep 2025 to Nov 2026. The hourly pattern **did not repeat**: the correlation between the two halves was 0.05. Going long in the 4 best hours from the first half lost **12.7%** after a 2 bp spread over 1,003 trades. Shorting the 4 worst hours lost **9.8%**. Weekday averages flip between 2006–2018 and 2019–2026. No timed up/down signal survived.

sections.title: 6. What this means for trading gold
sections.text:
- Use the **ranges** for stop and target placement, and **volatility sizing** for position size. Both held up on unseen data.
- Don't pay for direction calls. Ours failed the test, and most published 'accurate gold signals' are scored on the data they were built from.
- For holds longer than a few days, CFD financing is a large, certain cost. An ETF or physical gold is cheaper.
- Forward-test anything new in paper trading for 4–8 weeks before risking money.
